# Arūpāvacarakusala (Ds 2.1.3)
**ID:** Ds 2.1.3
**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Arūpāvacarakusala
**Title (English, from literature):** Good in Relation to the Universe of the Formless
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ds2.1.3
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh01m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Arūpāvacarakusala* constitutes the section on immaterial or formless-sphere wholesome states within the *cittuppādakaṇḍa* of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral; Rhys Davids 1900; Gethin 2001]. Following the treatments of wholesome consciousness belonging to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*) and the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*), it analyzes the wholesome dhammas pertaining to the formless realm (*arūpāvacara-kusala-citta*) [Rhys Davids 1900; Gethin 2001; Frauwallner 1995]. The exposition is structured around the four formless meditative attainments (*cattāri arūpajjhānāni*): the base of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), the base of infinite consciousness (*viññāṇañcāyatana*), the base of nothingness (*ākiñcaññāyatana*), and the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*) [Rhys Davids 1900; Bodhi 1999; Frauwallner 1995]. In classical Abhidhamma taxonomy, these four wholesome immaterial states constitute imperturbable kamma-formation (*āneñjābhisaṅkhāra*), functioning as the direct generative causes for rebirth in the four formless heavens (*arūpa-brahma*) [Van Gorkom 2009; Boriharnwanaket 2009].
SuttaCentral lists two modern translations in two languages and notes no direct historical parallels [SuttaCentral]. According to DharmaNexus, the text shares 429 matching passages across nine other Pali canonical works, reflecting extensive standardized formulaic reuse [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial internal reuse partners within the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī* are the adjacent *Rūpāvacarakusala* (Ds 2.1.2; 185 matches), *Abyākatavipāka* (Ds 2.1.7; 57 matches), and *Tebhūmakakusala* (Ds 2.1.4; 36 matches), together with analytical sections of the *Vibhaṅga*, such as the *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* (Vb 6), *Paṭisambhidāvibhaṅga* (Vb 15), and *Jhānavibhaṅga* (Vb 12) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text with Sanskrit and Tibetan Mahāyāna corpora—notably the Sanskrit *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* (13 matches) and Tibetan Prajñāpāramitā texts—reflecting formulaic terminological stock shared across Buddhist traditions concerning the four formless attainments [DharmaNexus].
